summary: The 10-file, 480-line stage remains a single CLI and repository-owner slice. The 550-line review budget explicitly accommodates the approved operator documentation and the atomic audit proof; no unrelated surface is admitted.
current_flow: The CLI resolves a hash-only access reference and delegates to the repository transaction, which activates the grant and records a safe recovery audit event. The bounded stage restores only CLI entry points, documentation, non-secret environment naming, architecture declarations, and focused tests.

criteria_map.gantry ui and gantry ui authorize create: CLI commands reuse existing local authorization and access-reference methods; approveAccessReference activates the grant and inserts auth.access.recovered within one transaction.
criteria_map.First-admin and lost-admin access refere: Existing hash-only, expiry-checked repository lookup remains authoritative.
criteria_map.OIDC candidate testing never changes act: Existing settings/auth services remain the sole candidate and activation owner; docs state the invariant.
criteria_map.Audit events cover login classification,: The existing event vocabulary is reused; CLI recovery adds only role and safe grant context through the transaction.
criteria_map.Docs cover local startup, hosted proxy a: The operations document covers all required operator flows.

rounds.question: Where must the recovery audit event be written to make it atomic with the grant?
Does this require a new generic audit abstraction?
options: Reuse runtime_events schema directly at the repository owner
rounds.chosen: Reuse runtime_events schema directly at the repository owner

citations.finding: CLI recovery must be audited without exposing secrets and must be transactional with approval.
